page: Amazon Web Services mac2-m2.metal is a bare-metal instance designed for Apple silicon macOS environments. It is powered by an Apple M2 processor built on the arm64_mac architecture, delivering 8 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.5 GHz. With one thread per core, the system provides 8 dedicated vCPUs without hyperthreading. System memory is fixed at 24.0 GB, providing an allocation of 3.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include discrete GPUs.

Networking performance is defined by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and the server includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Local storage is not provided, meaning the instance has no onboard NVMe or SSD capacity. As a result, operating system storage, application environments, and persistent assets rely entirely on network-attached storage options, making data throughput dependent on external network storage configuration.

The instance configuration maintains a 1:3 vCPU-to-RAM ratio on dedicated physical cores. This balance of dedicated hardware resources makes mac2-m2.metal suited for Apple ecosystem continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, Xcode software compilation, automated mobile application testing, and macOS-targeted build workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services mac2-m2.metal is a dedicated bare-metal server configured for macOS operations within AWS infrastructure. Built on the arm64_mac architecture, the instance incorporates an Apple processor featuring 8 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.5 GHz, mapping directly to 8 vCPUs with single-thread-per-core execution. System memory is allocated at 24.0 GB, yielding 3.0 GB per core. The instance does not include discrete GPUs and provides no onboard local storage, requiring network-attached storage for operating system images and persistent volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The balanced CPU and memory profile delivers dedicated hardware execution tailored for native Apple platform software builds, continuous integration pipelines, automated application testing, and macOS build farm deployments.
